questions.question: Your boyfriend wakes up with one unexpected free hour. What does he do first?
questions.hint: Free time is just an unannounced project deadline.

options.text: Make breakfast and enjoy a peaceful morning

reaction.title: TOO PEACEFUL.
reaction.body: A lovely fantasy. He has already opened three tabs and started investigating something.

options.text: Go back to sleep immediately

reaction.title: TEMPTING.
reaction.body: He considered it. Then an idea happened, which is worse.

options.text: Check his messages and accidentally lose the hour
Organize the entire day with a color-coded plan

reaction.title: AMBITIOUS.
reaction.body: He may create the plan. Following it is an entirely separate feature.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The free hour has been successfully converted into screen time.

questions.question: When your boyfriend says he is not hungry, what does he actually mean?
questions.hint: Watch what happens when somebody else opens a snack.

options.text: He genuinely is not hungry

reaction.title: UNSUPPORTED CLAIM.
reaction.body: The evidence does not support this. The evidence is currently looking at your snack.

options.text: He will be hungry in exactly five minutes

reaction.title: CLOSE.
reaction.body: Five minutes is optimistic. The snack detection system is faster than that.

options.text: He wants food but does not want to choose the food

reaction.title: PLAUSIBLE.
reaction.body: A strong theory, but the real answer involves a mysteriously empty packet.

options.text: He is not hungry until someone else has food

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Hunger has been activated by the presence of another person’s snack.

questions.question: Your boyfriend reads a message and does not reply. What is most likely happening?
questions.hint: Silence does not mean nothing is happening.

options.text: He forgot to reply

reaction.title: PARTLY TRUE.
reaction.body: He did not forget the message. He forgot the concept of replying.

options.text: He is writing the perfect response in his head
He is upset

reaction.title: DRAMATIC.
reaction.body: Not upset. Just mentally composing a reply that will now never leave the draft dimension.

options.text: His phone has entered a mysterious silent state

reaction.title: CONVENIENT.
reaction.body: The phone works. The notification was seen. The reply is trapped somewhere else.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The reply exists in his head and nowhere else.

questions.question: Your boyfriend needs to buy one thing from the store. How does the trip end?
questions.hint: The shopping list is only a suggestion.

options.text: He buys the one thing and comes straight home

reaction.title: FICTION.
reaction.body: A one-item trip is theoretically possible. It has never been observed here.

options.text: He returns with the one thing and three unrelated items
He forgets the one thing but buys a drink

reaction.title: A CLASSIC.
reaction.body: This has happened. But today he has evolved into a more expensive version of the problem.

options.text: He turns the errand into a full afternoon expedition

reaction.title: TOO MUCH.
reaction.body: That is the advanced form. This question is asking about the standard encounter.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The bonus items were not optional. They simply appeared.

questions.question: When your boyfriend asks what you want to do, what happens next?
questions.hint: He asked for an answer, not necessarily a decision.

options.text: He picks one of your suggestions immediately

reaction.title: SUSPICIOUS.
reaction.body: A decision that fast would trigger a security alert.

options.text: He says he is fine with anything, then rejects every option
He presents a carefully researched shortlist

reaction.title: LATER.
reaction.body: He may present a shortlist after the situation has become unnecessarily complicated.

options.text: He says the choice is yours and disappears

reaction.title: RUDE.
reaction.body: He remains physically present. His decision-making has disappeared.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. ‘Anything’ has been confirmed to mean ‘not those things’.

questions.question: A tiny household problem appears. What does your boyfriend do?
questions.hint: The original problem is rarely the final scope.

options.text: Fix it quickly with the simplest possible solution

reaction.title: NOT HIS BRAND.
reaction.body: The simplest solution has been rejected for lacking lore.

options.text: Ignore it until it becomes urgent

reaction.title: POSSIBLE, BUT NO.
reaction.body: He has noticed it. That means the situation is about to receive a system.

options.text: Research the problem until he understands its entire history

reaction.title: WARM.
reaction.body: Research is merely phase one. You have not yet accounted for the prototype.

options.text: Build a solution that is far more advanced than the problem

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The tiny problem now has documentation, settings, and a roadmap.

questions.question: How many browser tabs does your boyfriend consider a normal number?
questions.hint: The answer is not a number most browsers can display comfortably.

options.text: Three or four

reaction.title: ADORABLE.
reaction.body: That is a calm person’s browser. Your boyfriend’s browser has a weather system.

options.text: Ten, but only when he is researching something

reaction.title: UNDERCOUNTED.
reaction.body: Ten tabs is the loading screen before the real browser appears.

options.text: Enough tabs that the titles have become tiny symbols
One tab per finished task

reaction.title: THEORETICAL.
reaction.body: Finished tasks do not generate tabs. Unfinished ideas do.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The tabs are not open; they are a permanent habitat.

questions.question: Your boyfriend cannot find something that is directly in front of him. What happens?
questions.hint: He will search everywhere except the obvious place.

options.text: He checks the exact place where it should be

reaction.title: TOO LOGICAL.
reaction.body: That location is excluded because it is too obvious.

options.text: He asks Anuradha to find it

reaction.title: A VALID SYSTEM.
reaction.body: This is a proven backup protocol, but not the first response.

options.text: He declares the object missing and starts a wider investigation

reaction.title: PREMATURE ESCALATION.
reaction.body: The investigation begins after the room has been searched three times.

options.text: He looks everywhere, then discovers it was in his hand

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The object has been recovered from the hand that was searching for it.

questions.question: Your boyfriend says he will choose a movie quickly. What should you expect?
questions.hint: The selection process has multiple hidden stages.

options.text: A movie starts within five minutes

reaction.title: BOLD PREDICTION.
reaction.body: The streaming service has not even been opened yet.

options.text: He watches trailers for two hours and chooses nothing
He watches the same favorite movie again

reaction.title: THE SAFE ROUTE.
reaction.body: That is the emergency fallback after the two-hour selection ritual.

options.text: He asks you to choose while continuing to browse

reaction.title: ALSO POSSIBLE.
reaction.body: But tonight he has unlocked the director’s commentary for every trailer.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The movie was never the goal. The browsing was the event.

questions.question: Your boyfriend buys a new gadget. What happens before he uses it?
questions.hint: The box is only the beginning of the ceremony.

options.text: He reads the quick-start guide and begins

reaction.title: IMPOSSIBLE.
reaction.body: He has already found a 46-minute review video.

options.text: He watches reviews, comparisons, and teardown videos
He returns it because the box looked suspicious

reaction.title: TOO SOON.
reaction.body: The box must first be investigated from several camera angles.

options.text: He gives it to someone else to set up

reaction.title: OUT OF CHARACTER.
reaction.body: He would rather invent a setup process than outsource the experience.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The gadget has been reviewed before it has been switched on.

questions.question: At bedtime, your boyfriend suddenly remembers an idea. What happens?
questions.hint: Sleep is about to lose the negotiation.

options.text: He writes one note and goes to sleep

reaction.title: NICE TRY.
reaction.body: The note has become a diagram, and the diagram has become a prototype.

options.text: He forgets it by morning

reaction.title: NO.
reaction.body: He will remember the least useful detail at 3:17 AM.

options.text: He spends twenty minutes thinking about it

reaction.title: UNDERSTATED.
reaction.body: Twenty minutes is the advertised duration. The actual duration is classified.

options.text: He opens his phone and accidentally starts a midnight project

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The bedtime idea has been promoted to an active midnight operation.

questions.question: Your boyfriend sees a complicated group-chat discussion. What does he do?
questions.hint: He is not going to leave the thread with unanswered questions.

options.text: Mute it and move on

reaction.title: HE COULD.
reaction.body: But now he needs to know why everyone is wrong.

options.text: Read only the last message

reaction.title: DANGEROUS.
reaction.body: Context has been requested. He is traveling backward through 187 messages.

options.text: Ask what happened and wait for the summary

reaction.title: OUTSOURCED CONTEXT.
reaction.body: He does not trust a summary when primary sources are available.

options.text: Read the entire thread and reconstruct the timeline

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The group chat is now a historical document.

questions.question: When your boyfriend says ‘it is a long story,’ what does that usually mean?
questions.hint: You have time. The story has chapters.

options.text: He will give the short version

reaction.title: A TRAGIC MISREAD.
reaction.body: There is no short version. There are only deleted subplots.

options.text: He does not want to discuss it

reaction.title: WRONG.
reaction.body: He absolutely wants to discuss it. He has already opened the supporting evidence.

options.text: He will explain the key events in about five minutes

reaction.title: ADORABLE.
reaction.body: Five minutes is how long it takes to introduce the characters.

options.text: He is about to deliver a detailed documentary with side quests

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. The story has entered its extended edition.

questions.question: Your boyfriend says ‘this should be easy.’ What should Anuradha do?
questions.hint: Prepare emotionally and locate the charger.

options.text: Trust him completely and make no backup plan

reaction.title: DANGEROUS.
reaction.body: His confidence is genuine. The scope of the task is not.

options.text: Ask how many hours he has planned for it

reaction.title: A GOOD QUESTION.
reaction.body: Unfortunately, the answer will be ‘not many’ followed by a new complication.

options.text: Quietly prepare snacks and accept the timeline

reaction.title: WISE.
reaction.body: Very wise. But the canon response requires a little more emergency readiness.

options.text: Prepare for an all-night operation disguised as a quick task

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. ‘Easy’ has been logged as a high-risk forecast.

questions.question: After observing all of this, which description best fits your boyfriend?
questions.hint: The answer is affectionate, accurate, and slightly alarming.

options.text: A normal man who occasionally overthinks things

reaction.title: DENIED.
reaction.body: The evidence has exceeded ‘occasionally’ by several thousand percent.

options.text: A thoughtful nerd with too many hobbies

reaction.title: PARTIAL CREDIT.
reaction.body: Thoughtful and nerdy, yes. But the hobbies have become infrastructure.

options.text: A curious problem-solver who cannot leave anything at version one

reaction.title: ACCURATE, BUT INCOMPLETE.
reaction.body: That is the polite summary. The system requires the full diagnosis.

options.text: A lovable chaos engineer turning every tiny idea into a full-scale side quest

questions.correctFeedback: CORRECT. Diagnosis complete: lovable chaos engineer.

phantomQuestions.question: What is your boyfriend thinking right now?

options.text: A brilliant new idea
Food
Nothing at all
He refuses to disclose that information

phantomQuestions.reveal: THIS QUESTION IS NOT ANSWERABLE. His thoughts are protected by boyfriend encryption. You still selected an option. Fascinating.

phantomQuestions.question: Which project will your boyfriend definitely finish this week?

options.text: The newest one
The oldest one
The most practical one
The one he has not started yet

phantomQuestions.reveal: NONE OF THESE ARE SAFE ANSWERS. He may finish one, begin three more, and rename the folder. The quiz declines responsibility.

phantomQuestions.question: How long will your boyfriend’s ‘quick explanation’ take?

options.text: Two minutes
Ten minutes
Until the explanation is complete
There is no measurable unit

phantomQuestions.reveal: THE CORRECT ANSWER WAS TO PROTECT YOUR EVENING. There was no such option. The explanation has begun.

options.text: Only the essentials
One backup outfit
A charger and several cables
A portable command center for every possible scenario

new project
final project

Midnight exactly
Whenever the work is done
The moment after one last idea stops expanding

He gives a quick answer
He explains the main idea
